_comment: Evergreen guide topics, drafted 2 a day in order (each key only once). Add new topics at the end; never reuse a key.

guides.title: How to answer 'Tell me about yourself' as a fresher
guides.angle: A 60-second structure (present, past, why this role) with two worked examples: a B.Tech CSE student and a BCA graduate. Common mistakes like reciting the resume.

guides.title: Building a one-page resume when you have no work experience
guides.angle: Section order for freshers, how to turn college projects into bullet points with action + tool + result, what to drop (objective, hobbies list, photo).

guides.title: An off-campus job search plan for final-year students
guides.angle: A weekly routine: where to look, how many applications are realistic, tracking them, and following up without spamming HR.

guides.title: What an ATS actually checks in your resume
guides.angle: Plain explanation of applicant tracking systems: file format, headings, matching the job's wording honestly, and the myths (white text, keyword stuffing).

guides.title: What happens in a first technical interview for freshers
guides.angle: The usual rounds (online test, technical, HR), what each checks, and how to prepare for each in the two weeks before.

guides.title: College projects that make recruiters call back
guides.angle: What makes a project credible (real users, a problem it solves, code on GitHub, a short write-up), with three project ideas per track: web, data, Android.

guides.title: How to email HR about a job without sounding desperate
guides.angle: A short email structure, subject lines that get opened, when to attach a resume, and when to follow up once (and stop).

guides.title: Setting up a LinkedIn profile that works for freshers
guides.angle: Headline, About section, featured projects and how to ask for referrals politely — without paying for Premium.

guides.title: How much SQL a fresher actually needs for data and backend roles
guides.angle: The core queries interviewers ask (joins, group by, window basics), a 3-week practice plan, and free datasets to practise on.

guides.title: A realistic DSA preparation plan for service and product companies
guides.angle: Which topics matter for which kind of company, how many problems are enough, and how to revise instead of grinding endlessly.

guides.title: Clearing the aptitude round in campus and off-campus tests
guides.angle: The usual sections (quant, logical, verbal), time management per section, and a daily 30-minute practice routine.

guides.title: Group discussion rounds: what evaluators are really looking for
guides.angle: How to enter the discussion, add one new point, summarise well, and what loses marks (shouting, going off-topic).

guides.title: Common HR round questions and honest ways to answer them
guides.angle: Strengths and weaknesses, relocation, bond, 'why should we hire you', and how to answer gaps or backlogs truthfully.

guides.title: Turning an internship into a pre-placement offer
guides.angle: What managers notice in the first month, how to ask for feedback, documenting your work, and the conversation about a PPO.

guides.title: Where final-year students find real internships (and how to avoid fake ones)
guides.angle: Places to look, signs of an unpaid 'training' scam or fee-charging internship, and what a genuine offer letter includes.

guides.title: Spotting fake job offers before you pay or share documents
guides.angle: Red flags: registration fees, offers without interviews, personal Gmail IDs, pressure to pay for training or laptops. What to do if it happened.

guides.title: Understanding your CTC: what you actually take home
guides.angle: Break down CTC into basic, HRA, PF, bonuses and variable pay, with a simple example of monthly in-hand salary. Avoid quoting real company figures.

guides.title: Service company or product company for your first job?
guides.angle: Honest trade-offs: training, pay pattern, bonds, learning speed, and how to switch later. No rankings of named companies.

guides.title: Service agreements and bonds in fresher offers: what to check
guides.angle: What a bond clause usually says, questions to ask HR before signing, and why to read the exit terms. Not legal advice.

guides.title: Using GitHub so recruiters can see your work
guides.angle: Pinned repositories, a good README, commit history that looks real, and what not to upload (copied tutorials, secrets).

guides.title: A fresher's roadmap to a frontend developer job
guides.angle: HTML/CSS, JavaScript, one framework (React), and three portfolio projects, with a rough month-by-month plan.

guides.title: A fresher's roadmap to a backend developer job
guides.angle: One language (Java or Node.js), REST APIs, a database, authentication and deployment basics, with project ideas.

guides.title: How freshers get into data analyst roles
guides.angle: Excel, SQL, one BI tool and Python basics; building two analysis case studies; what analyst interviews test.

guides.title: Starting a career in software testing as a fresher
guides.angle: Manual testing basics, test cases, one automation tool, and why QA can be a strong first role rather than a fallback.

guides.title: Cloud and DevOps for freshers: what to learn first
guides.angle: Linux, Git, one cloud's core services, Docker basics and CI, with a small deploy-your-own-project exercise.

guides.title: Getting an IT job from a non-CS branch
guides.angle: Mechanical, civil, ECE or BSc students: picking one track, proving skills with projects, and explaining the switch in interviews.

guides.title: Job hunting with backlogs or a year gap
guides.angle: Which applications to prioritise, how to explain it honestly in one line, and what to do with the gap time now.

guides.title: Asking for a referral without knowing anyone
guides.angle: Finding alumni, a short referral request message, making it easy to say yes, and thanking people either way.

guides.title: Checking an offer letter before you accept
guides.angle: Role, CTC breakup, joining date, probation, notice period, bond and documents asked for — and how to ask questions politely.

guides.title: What to do when your joining date keeps getting delayed
guides.angle: Staying in touch with HR, keeping applying meanwhile, and how to handle a better offer that comes during the wait.

guides.title: Practising interviews alone or with friends
guides.angle: Recording yourself, a peer mock-interview format, a question bank by round, and how to review your answers.

guides.title: Improving spoken English for interviews in 30 days
guides.angle: Daily speaking practice, structuring answers, handling nervousness, and why clarity beats fancy vocabulary.

guides.title: Which certifications actually help freshers get hired
guides.angle: When a certificate helps (cloud, specific tools) and when a project helps more; free vs paid; avoid naming exam prices.

guides.title: Online coding tests: how they work and how to prepare
guides.angle: Proctoring rules, partial test cases, time limits, choosing a language, and practising under test conditions.

guides.title: Your first week at your first job
guides.angle: Questions to ask your manager, taking notes, setting up your work, and building a good reputation early.

guides.title: Remote jobs for freshers: realistic or not?
guides.angle: Where genuine remote fresher roles come from, why they are competitive, and scams that pose as remote work.

guides.title: Resume mistakes that quietly get freshers rejected
guides.angle: Spelling, unprofessional email IDs, vague bullets, fake skills, wrong file names — each with a quick fix.

guides.title: Tailoring your resume to each job without lying
guides.angle: Reordering skills, rewording bullets to the job's language, choosing which projects to show — and what never to add.

guides.title: Can a fresher negotiate salary? Sometimes — here's how
guides.angle: When there is room (competing offers, specialised skills), how to ask politely, and when to accept the standard offer.

guides.title: Skills most asked for in fresher jobs this month
guides.angle: Built entirely from the live GeeksFinder job data in the facts list: the top skills, cities and roles, and what students can do with this.
